title: Graceful Degradation Orchestrator: Design, Telemetry Contract, and Validation
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Purpose

This document defines the Graceful Degradation Orchestrator (GDO): the runtime subsystem that coordinates fidelity reduction, kernel variant switching, and routing fallbacks when capacity, thermal/power or kernel regressions threaten SLOs. It specifies the telemetry contract between the orchestrator and downstream subsystems (scheduler, kernel mapper, network router, kv-cache and model manager), describes configuration primitives, and provides a validation and incident-runbook for operators.

Summary (short)

- Why: Keep customer-facing latency and success-rate SLOs while minimizing cost and output-quality regression during resource-constrained events.
- What: A declarative orchestrator that synthesizes signals and executes a prioritized set of mitigation actions (local kernel switch, model fidelity stepdown, prioritized admission, cross-region reroute).
- Who: Owned by eng-serving-runtime (scheduler + runtime-ops collaboration).
- When to use: automatically in production via policies; manually for targeted customers via orchestration console.

Design goals

1) SLO-first: Preserve p50/p95 latency objectives and success-rate (generation completion) where possible.
2) Observable: Every mitigation must emit structured telemetry and be reversible.
3) Progressive fidelity: Minimize perceptible quality regression by ordering mitigations from least-visible to most-visible.
4) Safe and auditable: All policy changes are versioned and subject to canary gates.

Key terms

- Fidelity step: Discrete quality reduction (e.g., int8 quantized variant, sequence-length cap, sampling temperature clamp, max_tokens cap, offload to smaller model).
- Kernel variant: Implementation variant of an operator (tensor-core optimized vs. scalar fallback).
- Mitigation action: Single atomic change that the orchestrator can apply and revert.
- Mitigation plan: Ordered list of mitigation actions with exit criteria.

Architecture overview

Components and interactions (high level)

- GDO controller (stateless service)
  - Receives aggregated signals and policy input.
  - Plans and issues actions via runtime control-plane APIs.

- Signal ingestion (streaming)
  - High-frequency telemetry from scheduler, kernel telemetry, GPU power/thermal, model-serving trace.
  - Low-frequency business signals: customer tier, active QBR or experiments.

- Execution agents (on-node agents)
  - Apply kernel switches, update config flags, trigger model variant swap, adjust admission tokens.

- Audit & Reconciliation service
  - Records planned vs applied actions, detects drift and attempts automated revert if mismatches persist.

Sequence diagram (textual)

1) Telemetry breach detected (p95 latency > 1.2x SLO for 30s)
2) GDO evaluates candidate mitigations based on policy and current state
3) GDO issues an optimistically-scoped mitigation (e.g., drop kernel launch priority; enable kernel low-latency codepath)
4) Observability checks evaluate effect for 20s; if improved -> commit; else escalate to next mitigation (e.g., quantized model variant or sequence-length cap)
5) If a mitigation causes quality regression beyond policy thresholds, revert and try alternative path or route to dedicated capacity tier.

Policy primitives (JSON example)

```json
{
  "policy_id": "gd-policy-2025-01",
  "priority": 100,
  "target_scope": {
    "model_id": "redwood-llama-70b-cpu-fallback",
    "tenant_ids": ["*"],
    "region": "us-west-2"
  },
  "slo_constraints": {
    "p95_latency_ms": 250,
    "success_rate": 0.995
  },
  "mitigation_plan": [
    {"action": "kernel_priority_tweak","params": {"kernel_id": "attn_v2","priority": "lower"},"exit_on": {"p95_latency_ms": 1.05}},
    {"action": "enable_kernel_variant","params": {"kernel_id": "attn_v2","variant": "nvcc_fast_f32"}},
    {"action": "fidelity_step","params": {"step": "quantize_int8"},"quality_guard": {"semantic-preservation": 0.92}},
    {"action": "limit_sequence_length","params": {"max_tokens": 256}},
    {"action": "route_to_dedicated","params": {"pool": "dedicated-500g"}}
  ]
}
```
Telemetry contract (signals, semantics, retention)

Table: signal -> producer -> semantics -> recommended sampling

| signal | producer | semantics | sampling |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| kernel_queue_depth | node-scheduler | number of pending kernel launches | 1s aggregated per node |
| token_emit_latency_ms | kernel-runtime | per-token emit time (median/95) | 1s sliding, store 30d aggregated |
| kernel_variant_switch_latency_ms | node-agent | time to move to variant and stabilize | report per switch (trace) |
| gpu_power_watts | hw-metrics | instantaneous power draw | 5s avg, store 90d samples |
| kvcache_hit_rate | kv-cache | fraction of requests served from persistent cache | 10s aggregate |
| request_failure_rate | api-gateway | fraction of requests that failed before completion | 1s aggregate |

Contract rules (plain language)

- All signals must include: timestamp (RFC3339), node_id, shard_id (if applicable), model_id, request_cohort (experimental/dedicated/hosted).
- Signal producers must maintain >= 30s retention in hot storage for high-frequency signals used by GDO decision window.
- Each mitigation action must emit a START/END event with correlation_id and pre/post snapshot of the small set of signals (queue_depth, p95 token emit latency, kvcache_hit_rate).

Mitigation action taxonomy and safe limits

- Non-invasive (fast revert): kernel priority tweak, scheduler backpressure adjustments, queue preemption. (Immediate revert safe)
- Moderate (short-term quality impact): change kernel variant to lower-latency optimized build, apply small quantization profile. (Guarded by sampling)
- Invasive (visible quality impact): hard sequence-length cap, route significant traffic to smaller model. (Require reviewer approval when touching enterprise tiers)

Table: action -> visible impact -> max duration (auto) -> revert criteria

| action | impact | max_auto_duration | revert_criteria |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| kernel_priority_tweak | none | 300s | no improvement in p95 after 30s |
| enable_kernel_variant | low | 600s | token error rate > 0.1% or p95 worsens 10% |
| fidelity_step (quantize) | medium | 900s | semantic_preservation_score < policy threshold |
| limit_sequence_length | high | 1800s | business metric drop > 2% |

Validation and preflight suite

Preflight tests that must pass before enabling a mitigation policy in production:

1) Canary microbenchmark: apply mitigation to a 1% shadow of production (shadow-not-serve) and evaluate p50/p95 and semantic-preservation (using an automated prompt set).
2) Regression fuzz: run a synthetic workload shaped to the target tenant's recent traffic (sequence-length distribution, tokens per request) and measure kernel stability for 10 minutes.
3) Stability soak: ensure no memory leaks or steady-state increased memory usage over 30 minutes.

CLI snippets (examples for operators)

- List active policies

$ rdoctl policies list --region us-west-2 --format table

- Trigger policy dry-run (canary 1%):

$ rdoctl policies apply --policy gd-policy-2025-01 --canary 0.01 --dry-run

- Force revert mitigation on node

$ rdoctl nodes revert-mitigation --node node-15 --correlation-id abcd-1234

Quality and semantic-preservation checks

- Redwood uses an internal prompt-set for fidelity checks. For GDO policy changes that perform quantization or model swaps, require the semantic_preservation metric to be >= 0.90 for public tiers and >= 0.95 for enterprise-tier policies.
- Semantic preservation is computed as: 1 - (normalized embedding distance between golden and mitigated outputs) aggregated across the prompt set.

Observability & dashboards

Minimum required dashboards for GDO operations:

- Mitigation action timeline: list of START/END events with correlated latency and success_rate lines.
- Quality delta panel: semantic_preservation over time split by tenant tier.
- Signal heatmap: token_emit_latency_ms p95 across nodes with kernel variants annotated.

Runbook: Incident triage (SRE playbook)

1) Alert: GDO escalates with priority P1 if p95 latency > 1.3x SLO and mitigation plan reaches invasive actions.
2) Immediate steps (0-5m):
   - Verify alert in dashboards.
   - Check GDO decision log (correlation_id) and list of applied mitigations.
   - If mitigation was applied in last 60s, run quick revert for the latest action and observe impact.
3) Next steps (5-20m):
   - If revert improves latency, keep reverted state and schedule a targeted canary for alternatives.
   - If revert does not help, escalate to runtime kernel leads and consider cross-region routing.
4) Recovery and postmortem (post 2 hours):
   - Record timeline events, include all START/END and signal snapshots.
   - Run semantic-preservation audits for any automatic quantize actions.
   - Publish RCA and update policy safe limits if necessary.

Safety and governance

- Enterprise customer exemptions: Policies that change model fidelity for enterprise customers must include an "exempt" flag in the policy or have an explicit allowlist.
- Change control: All policy edits are audited and require a single-engineering approval and a product reviewer for changes that alter semantic thresholds.

Testing & benchmarking guidance

- Use the benchmarking suite to generate a representative request corpus (see service-profile builder). For each mitigation candidate:
  - Measure delta_p95 and delta_semantic_preservation over 10k requests.
  - Measure CPU/GPU utilization and memory delta for each node type.
  - Produce a mitigation scorecard: {p95_delta_pct, sem_pres_mean, cost_delta_pct}.

Appendix A: Example mitigation scorecard (table)

| mitigation | p95_delta_pct | sem_pres_mean | cost_delta_pct |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| kernel_priority_tweak | -8 | 0.99 | -0.5 |
| enable_kernel_variant nvcc_fast_f32 | -12 | 0.995 | +1.2 |
| quantize_int8 (aggressive) | -25 | 0.88 | -33 |

Appendix B: Correlation IDs and event schema (example)

Event payload (single line JSON for logs):

{"ts":"2025-11-01T16:24:32Z","correlation_id":"gdo-7f4a","node_id":"node-15","action":"quantize","phase":"start","policy_id":"gd-policy-2025-01","snapshot":{"p95_token_ms":312,"kvcache_hit":0.62}}

Appendix C: Ownership and contacts

- Primary owner: eng-serving-runtime (runtime-ops subteam)
- Oncall escalation: runtime-oncall -> runtime-kernel-rotation -> eng-sre
- Design/approvals: Marco Reyes (kernel lead) and Jordan Kim (runtime infrastructure)

Notes and future work

- Integrate language-model-aware quality metrics (hallucination detection) to make quality_guard criteria more robust.
- Add ML-driven mitigation ranking (currently rule-based) to reduce human tuning.
- Expose a per-tenant simulation sandbox in the Console for product and CS to preview potential mitigations.
